title: Conservative Contextual Bandits: Beyond Linear Representations

contributions.purpose: Enable conservative (safety-constrained) contextual bandits for general non-linear cost functions, which prior UCB-based methods (limited to multi-armed and linear settings) could not handle.
contributions.mechanism: C-SquareCB: reduce the conservative bandit problem to a black-box online regression oracle with squared loss, using Inverse Gap Weighting (IGW) exploration and switching to the baseline action when a safety condition is violated. Novel analysis bounds n_T (times baseline is played) by relating it to squared regression loss instead of UCB confidence sets.
contributions.evaluation: Proves regret O(sqrt(K T Reg_Sq(T)) + K Reg_Sq(T)/alpha) with the (1+alpha) performance constraint satisfied w.h.p. (Theorem 3.1).
contributions.source_quote: Reduction using Squared loss: We provide an algorithm for conservative bandits for general cost functions using an oracle for online regression with squared loss (see Algorithm 1). We subsequently prove a O(sqrt(KT Reg_Sq(T)) + K Reg_Sq(T)/alpha) regret bound... and also ensure that the performance constraint is satisfied in high probability (see Theorem 3.1).

contributions.purpose: Obtain a sharper, data-dependent (first-order) regret guarantee for conservative bandits that scales with the optimal policy's cumulative loss L* rather than horizon T.
contributions.mechanism: C-FastCB: reduce to an online regression oracle with KL loss, with an episodic, time-dependent exploration parameter gamma_t (constant within each of log(L*) episodes) to avoid a sqrt(T) dependence.
contributions.evaluation: Proves first-order regret O(sqrt(K L* log(L*) Reg_KL(T)) + K Reg_KL(T)(1+1/alpha)) with performance constraint satisfied w.h.p. (Theorem 4.1).
contributions.source_quote: Reduction using KL loss: Next, we provide an algorithm using an oracle for online regression with KL loss (see Algorithm 2) and prove a [first order] regret bound... This is a first order regret bound and is data-dependent in the sense that it scales with the cumulative cost of the best policy L*, instead of the horizon length T.

contributions.purpose: Provide concrete end-to-end guarantees by instantiating the abstract oracle with a neural network, and validate empirically.
contributions.mechanism: Instantiate the online regression oracle with Online Gradient Descent (OGD) over a feed-forward neural network, leveraging O(log T) neural-regression regret; then benchmark on real-world data.
contributions.evaluation: End-to-end bounds ~O(sqrt(KT)+K/alpha) (Thm 5.1) and ~O(sqrt(K L*)+K(1+1/alpha)) (Thm 5.2). On openml multiclass-classification bandit datasets (averaged over 10 runs), C-SquareCB and C-FastCB show sub-linear regret and beat the C-LinUCB baseline while keeping constraint-violation percentage low; C-FastCB does better on some datasets due to its first-order guarantee.
contributions.source_quote: Regret Bounds using Neural Networks: We instantiate the online regression oracle with Online Gradient Descent (OGD) and the function approximator with a feed-forward neural network to give an end-to-end regret bound... Experiments: Finally, we compare our proposed algorithms with existing baselines for conservative bandits and show that our algorithms consistently perform better.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Distinct from the previous set of works, Foster & Rakhlin (2020) and Foster & Krishnamurthy (2021) developed general reductions from the bandit problem to online regression using the Inverse Gap Weighting (IGW) idea... This reduction works for general cost functions and uses only a mild realizability assumption.

Such a conservative bandit formulation has been studied in the multi-armed setting (Wu et al., 2016) and the contextual linear setting (Kazerouni et al., 2017; Garcelon et al., 2020), but algorithms and regret guarantees for the general case do not exist.

The analysis in Foster & Rakhlin (2020) does not have a safety condition and therefore our analysis bounding n_T (the number of times the baseline action is played) in Step 2 and the performance constraint satisfaction in Step 4 of proof of Theorem 3.1 are original contributions... In the linear case (Kazerouni et al., 2017), the analysis crucially uses the upper and lower confidence bounds for the parameter estimates.

notes: Theory paper; contributions are two new algorithms + neural instantiation + experiments. No negative or tie results - experiments claim consistent wins over C-LinUCB baseline while maintaining the safety constraint. The paper is explicit that it extends the IGW reduction of Foster & Rakhlin (2020) / Foster & Krishnamurthy (2021) to the conservative/safe setting and generalizes the linear conservative analysis of Kazerouni et al. (2017); the n_T bounding technique (relating to regression loss rather than UCB confidence sets) is flagged as the original piece.
